scope_amendments.authorized_by: User-confirmed lead decision for completion Task 11.
scope_amendments.reason: Task 11 composes the outbox route that turns a written memory into a governed embedding delivery job, and Task 10's adoption materializes a memory revision's content the same way. Both need a content material owned by a memory revision. MaterialKeyCreationIntent pairs a free-form owner_kind with an owner_id typed PrincipalId: the type was fitted to its first and only user, provider_result, which is genuinely owned by a principal, and never generalized. A second owner kind cannot be expressed without storing a revision id in a PrincipalId, which would leave a value in the domain that is not what its type says it is. owner_id becomes a Uuid paired with the owner_kind that decides what it names, matching the column it has always been written to. The blast radius is one construction site and two readers, all three named here; no behaviour, migration or guarded authority changes.

scope_amendments.authorized_by: User-confirmed lead decision for completion Task 11.

scope_amendments.authorized_by: User-confirmed lead decision for completion Task 14: expand scope and carry activation through.
scope_amendments.reason: Embedding transition activation has been unreachable for the whole package, and the cause is in this file. Migration 0197 line 147 requires a canonical registration's returned_model to equal its model revision's wire_model_id, and this fixture declares two different models for one job: the model revision is inserted with wire_model_id 'embedding-model', while acceptance_command declares response_model RESULT_MODEL, which is 'text-embedding-nomic-embed-text-v1.5'. The result chain compares the dispatch request's model against what the outputs declared and the canonical registration against the wire model, so a job from this fixture can satisfy one or the other and never both. Registered under the wire model the canonical space refuses the fixture's results with EMBEDDING_RESULT_CONFLICT; registered under RESULT_MODEL the space is refused at registration with 23514. Consequently no fixture-built delivery job can land outputs in a canonical space, no transition over one can be activated, every call to vestrace_activate_embedding_transition in the repository is an unwrap_err, and Task 14's mutations 8 and 9 -- both inside that authority -- cannot be qualified. The amendment unifies the two strings onto RESULT_MODEL. Measured before requesting it: the only other files naming 'embedding-model' are embedding_data_policy, embedding_carry_classification, model_request_evidence, provider_dispatch_is_atomic and embedding_dispatch_crash, and all of them still pass on the unified fixture (model_request_evidence keeps its one pre-existing 55006 failure, unchanged). No further path is therefore added. No protected authority path changes; protected_authority_paths remains 23. scope_amendments.reason: Two of the eight red suites fail in their own setup rather than on the product, and both repairs are confined to the test file. expired_check_cannot_omit_a_live_governed_input_without_bytes deliberately corrupts content_material_bytes by disabling its guards, deleting a row as the guarded owner and re-enabling them. ENABLE TRIGGER fails with 55006 cannot ALTER TABLE because it has pending trigger events. The amendment disables and re-enables that third trigger alongside the other two, symmetric with what the fixture already does, so the test reaches the assertion it was written for: the expired check is refused with 23514 and writes no rows. It is a fixture that never saw 0194, not a defect in 0194. loopback_observes_semantic_equality_with_the_production_adapter answers its own /embeddings request with a hardcoded body carrying no model field and one vector for a two-input request. The amendment derives the stub's answer from the request it received, model echoed and one vector per input, so it cannot drift out of agreement with the adapter again the way a hardcoded literal did. scope_amendments.authorized_by: User-confirmed lead decision, in answer to the finding, to close the delivery/rebuild XOR for real rather than retire the test that caught it.
scope_amendments.reason: Task 5 was asked for a closed delivery/rebuild acceptance XOR and produced an open one. 0199 lines 138-158 widened sixteen authorities by blanket lexical substitution, turning every kind='delivery' into kind IN ('delivery','rebuild') and every kind<>'delivery' into kind NOT IN ('delivery','rebuild'). That is the right rewrite for a check asking whether this is one of the two kinds a path serves, and the wrong one for a check asking whether this is the kind THIS path serves, and the substitution could not tell them apart. Two holes resulted, one at each end of the XOR. vestrace_begin_delivery_embedding_outputs validated only that the declared kind was one of the two legal words, and the declared word then became the job: the receipt carries it and vestrace_finalize_delivery_embedding_outputs passes it into vestrace_accept_embedding_job, which writes embedding_jobs.kind. So a caller could mint a rebuild out of nothing. And vestrace_create_embedding_transition_batch_attempt at 0200 line 754 admitted both kinds, so an ordinary delivery could satisfy a transition recipe -- and a satisfied recipe is what activation moves the corpus head on. 0207 closes both against a fact that already exists and is already relied on: a rebuild serves a transition, and the one production rebuild path, legacy adoption, already refuses a target space that no transition plan names. A transition attempt now requires job kind rebuild; a rebuild acceptance now requires a transition plan targeting its space. What 0207 deliberately does not refuse is a delivery whose space happens to be a transition target, because the target space becomes the head after activation and refusing ordinary writes to it would be a rule invented here rather than one the product already holds. The replacements are anchored substitutions rather than retyped bodies, because both functions are long and a retyped body can silently drop a line; but unlike 0199 each anchor must occur exactly once in exactly one named function, and each result is read back before the migration is allowed to finish. That precondition earned itself immediately: the first anchor matched twice, because the four-space form is a substring of the eight-space form in the insert-race branch, and the migration refused instead of substituting into the wrong place. What this cost in fixtures is the finding rather than a side effect. Every transition attempt in embedding_transition_activation drove the machinery with delivery jobs, and the executor's rebuild fixture minted a rebuild on a plain space with no transition at all. Nine tests across three files plus one fault scenario were building a fiction that nothing contradicted. Each now plans its transition first and accepts a rebuild for it, which is the order production works in. prepare_rebuild_job also reads the job kind back and asserts it, because a fixture that believes it built a rebuild and built a delivery is exactly how the open XOR survived a whole package. Runs: embedding_transition_activation 14/14 including the new a_transition_attempt_refuses_a_delivery_job_standing_in_for_a_rebuild, embedding_executor 2/2, embedding_output_keys 28/28, embedding_fault_scenario_e2e 6/6 with --ignored, cargo build -p vestrace-fault-scenario clean. embedding_output_keys::invalid_delivery_authority_and_output_identity_matrix_rolls_back_wholly was one of the 24 standing red tests and is green here: it was a real defect rather than debt, so the standing figure becomes 23. No protected authority path changes; protected_authority_paths remains 23. The frozen contract baseline is not recaptured: head, dirty_files, status_porcelain_v1_z_base64, status_porcelain_v1_z_sha256, and all 126 historical migration digests through 0196 are unchanged.

scope_amendments.authorized_by: User-confirmed lead decision to take apart the nine untouched red tests on the embedding dispatch path.
scope_amendments.reason: The dispatch atomicity suite's nine red tests were described as three causes on the strength of their error text, and they are one. Migration 0194 forward-replaced vestrace_lock_embedding_job_pre_dispatch_gate so that a requested or running embedding job must carry a nonempty, complete, exact receipted output set before it can be dispatched; the pre-0194 body only refused a job whose material intents existed but were unconfigured. That gate is called from three places -- vestrace_lock_provider_dispatch_routing at 0192 line 590, vestrace_try_admit_provider_dispatch at 0192 line 946, and vestrace_lock_embedding_job_recovery_authority at 0187 line 842 -- and the adapter maps its 23514 differently at each: map_routing_error yields Policy PROVIDER_DISPATCH_ROUTING_REFUSED, map_embedding_job_recovery_error yields Conflict the embedding job is not in a recoverable governed state, and the admission path surfaces the raw 23514. One refusal, three names, and the three names were counted as three causes. Reading the messages was better than reading a remembered summary, but a message is still a symptom. The suite builds P03's bare accepted job -- accept_embedding_job creates the embedding_jobs row with no outputs at all -- and since 0194 that job is undispatchable and unrecoverable by construction. It cannot be repaired by adding outputs afterwards either: an already accepted bare job cannot be backfilled with guessed identities, which is the rule the fault-scenario fixture already documents in a comment. So the repair starts from the pre-acceptance boundary and lets accept_delivery_outputs fix the job and its outputs in one transaction, exactly as production does. dispatchable_embedding_job and its credential-branch sibling do that: pre-acceptance job, three live sources attached to the evidence, make_dispatchable, accept_delivery_outputs, reconcile_output_receipts. No delivery policy decision is recorded, because the pre-dispatch gate does not read one -- that is a result-preparation concern -- and recording it needs the provisioner-installed database this suite does not use. Five of the eight are green on that alone, including an_embedding_job_dispatches_through_the_shared_authority, which is the oracle clause 935 rests on. The suite goes from 13 passed 9 failed to 18 passed 4 failed, and none of the thirteen that already passed was disturbed. Three remain, and they revealed a further real rule rather than a fixture accident: vestrace_terminate_embedding_job_pre_dispatch refuses a cancellation unless every output material intent is abandoned with its exact witness. A job with no outputs never met that rule because it never had to; a job with outputs must retire them first. Those three need the output-retirement path built into the fixture through request_retirement and record_retirement, and they are left red rather than worked around. The ninth test, the_model_data_policy_leg_is_absent_from_an_embedding_dispatch, is unrelated to all of this: it asserts against itself that BeforePolicyRecord is on the dispatch path and the atomicity test does not yet cover it, which is the uncovered fault point already recorded in this document. No product change. No protected authority path changes; protected_authority_paths remains 23. The frozen contract baseline is not recaptured: head, dirty_files, status_porcelain_v1_z_base64, status_porcelain_v1_z_sha256, and all 126 historical migration digests through 0196 are unchanged.
